## Design

### 2026-10-20 – Day 1 Week 3 - MIDI beginnings

**3h**

Day 1 Week 3 - MIDI beginnings

Today, I started work on my MIDI keypad. After importing the footprints, began a long session of thinking, how can I make this project uniquely me? I decided to add some additional features, and actually dabble in software this time. The project said you can have different components, so I decided to go with an OLED screen, a rotary encoder with a switch, and capacitive touch keys. For the interface, I'm thinking of going for something like MusicDJ on those old, pre I-Phone Sony Ericssons.

![images](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/5Di8qxPvTjh464E0buJSS1rL8xZfVQiB/23ea89605147c3c8aded89fe1f1ee61ef72070c5092c98867d89437234c05705.png)

Unfortunately, I didn't get to play with KiCad and the actual PCB designing now, but what I have done, is choose which board I want, the ESP32-S3-ZERO,

![Screenshot 2026-10-19 235941](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/5Di8qxPvTjh464E0buJSS1rL8xZfVQiB/bbd5c1aafe45086a38ad2318c39ca0e3f265b76d9c42543b266d253641c419d4.png)

and added my components to the schematic.

![Screenshot 2026-10-20 000551](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/5Di8qxPvTjh464E0buJSS1rL8xZfVQiB/baddf8c38789a145bb3d2f30d148096f05ea7ccae2f89fb6992358fc40a4a142.png)

PCB design isn't going to go as fast as before because I also have to work on the software for this thing. That's all for now. Cheers!

### 2026-10-21 – Day 2 Week 3 - Finishing the PCB

**3h**

Day 2 Week 3 - Finishing the PCB

Today I finished the schematic and PCB, the next stuff from here is software, and minor fixes / modifications. I picked up from last time, realizing only that KiCad had an error and I had to start all over again. That's fine. I didn't have much progress anyway. I placed down all the components and traces, along with labels in order to make sure everything connected. Afterwards, I assigned footprints, and then the schematic turned out well.

Schematic:

![Screenshot 2026-10-20 224152](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/5Di8qxPvTjh464E0buJSS1rL8xZfVQiB/3a6830c9e54962ee6ba71ee19e00a1306baace8800dc37b175cfebba6989e3b9.png)

Next, I laid out the basic components of the PCB, and following the tutorial, had to create the footprint for the capacitive touchpads for the keys. It wasn't that hard, I just created 7 rectangles, although I might improve on it later.

Footprint:

![image_2026-10-20_235913045](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/5Di8qxPvTjh464E0buJSS1rL8xZfVQiB/487414a927010e4cba68971b37ef83dbd2896da81953a2f44d5e4955026972bc.png)

Finally, I added the schematic to the PCB editor, and created the general layout. Adding traces was easy, which was surprising from last time... Anyway, the PCB is done. All I need to do from here is software. I might update the board, add some small storage, or wire the switch for the rotary encoder. I need to do this while "budgeting" for the pins on the PCB.

PCB:

![Screenshot 2026-10-20 234637](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/5Di8qxPvTjh464E0buJSS1rL8xZfVQiB/71e9a174976d40ce3f587f3c6bd0419a28f4d0b04a383433262fe2a2d88e84b9.png)

### 2026-10-23 – I started working on code and wired up the switch of the rotary encoder to the ESP32.

**3h**

I started working on code and wired up the switch of the rotary encoder to the ESP32.

I began by looking over what I had before, and seeing what I had to do next. I began by downloading the code off of the Github Repo and adding it to the project.

Downloaded code:

![Screenshot 2026-10-22 214336](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/5Di8qxPvTjh464E0buJSS1rL8xZfVQiB/d37ecb20e2e259b8c09c9b5fe28d331e6417cac061b1f32130ed4558d90f2678.png)

After that, I opened it in Cursor and began describing what I want. First, before making any code, I want a simulator to see anything wrong with the Python code, since, obviously, I don't have the hardware yet. While it was doing that I jotted down what I want the code to be. A MusicDJ-like application where you can swap through instruments, place down notes, and scroll across the trackbar.

Cursor shenanignans:

![Screenshot 2026-10-22 220221](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/5Di8qxPvTjh464E0buJSS1rL8xZfVQiB/3b207b3c5a85a1b0abb4f8550740b2c3c7bc5b3aa71224c7439cb3386591b64c.png)

Finally, while Cursor was doing it's thing, I went back into the editor and just routed the rotary encoder's switch to the ESP-32. It was a simple fix that didn't take any time.

Switch routed:

![image_2026-10-22_222300491](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/5Di8qxPvTjh464E0buJSS1rL8xZfVQiB/95fe840251090db2146b6de646d36dbf1ac6f952f549fa388ef42a6ce8ec05ad.png)

For the future, I will finish the software and might add an SD card reader to export/save composed midis. Cheers!

### 2026-10-24 – Day 5 Week 3

**3h**

Day 5 Week 3
Today, I finished the software for the Midi Keypad. It took quite a while and a LOT of documentation-reading and work. I decided to "dumb-down" my idea, as I realized that I wouldn't be able to complete it with my Python/circuit coding skills. I started by looking over the existing code and seeing what Cursor had done. I looked up the documentation for the libraries included, and began to think. I'm just going to have the rotary encoder change instruments, while the keypad plays the notes of that instrument, and the OLED acts as a Windows Media player... visualizer... thing... Anyway, I hopped onto coding.

Me reading the documentation:

![Screenshot 2026-10-23 215556](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/5Di8qxPvTjh464E0buJSS1rL8xZfVQiB/b4bea4ad52c4a201e30beb32539e210a10bfc55b290920f215175c4e588b0087.png)

Coding was going mostly well, and I learned quite a bit about how computers work with circuits. Before this, I had hand-coded stuff for other computers, like small games, websites, etc. When AI came around, I tried it out and was immediately fascinated, and from there I've been working with AI, so this was a nice little refresher. In my opinion, your programming journey should start with learning basic languages (Python, HTML, etc.) to learn about how computers work and think. From there, you should add small snippets of AI in the code to learn how AI interacts with the code you've written, then use tools like Cursor from there and learn how to vibe-code, while still leaving enough human touches to make a good product.

My programming, with some assistance:

![Screenshot 2026-10-23 215449](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/5Di8qxPvTjh464E0buJSS1rL8xZfVQiB/3cb21eac2e1b47c38b4b466d1e16ac54a431b0881aa181b537367a107a3d2c0d.png)

Anyway, enough yapping. Midway throughout the programming, I used the simulator that Cursor wrote last session to see what I needed and if it would work on real hardware. The reports came back and it turned out I needed to include 2 libraries to make the visualizer work. adafruit_displayio_ssd1306  and adafruit_midi. Yay, a painful rewrite! It took a long time of thinking, reading, checking what went wrong, parsing through errors, consulting the simulation, and looking through documentation to see what went wrong. However, I prevailed, and finally, the code finally ran though, and would work on the display.

My import:
![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/5Di8qxPvTjh464E0buJSS1rL8xZfVQiB/5668fe7be70112f4ee4859e7d9c903cb7394829bda451a093fb56edb0bc582fc.png)

From here, I'm going to finish the BOM, commit, and push to git, then I'm done for the week.
